newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-MUSHTAQ SPINS PAKISTAN TO 11-RUN VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MUSHTAQ SPINS PAKISTAN TO 11-RUN VICTORY.

text.p: Off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq claimed five for 44 on Wednesday to spin Pakistan to an 11-run victory over New Zealand in the opening one-day international.
The 20-year-old returned his best figures in limited overs cricket as the New Zealanders, chasing Pakistan's 228 for eight in 46 overs, were dismissed for 217 in 45.4 overs.
Mushtaq, whose previous best was four for 28 against Zimbabwe, dismantled the brittle New Zealand batting to put his side 1-0 up in the three-match series.
Opener Bryan Young was top scorer for the tourists with a fluent 58 off 93 balls containing three fours while Stephen Fleming and Chris Cairns contributed 36 each and Adam Parore scored 35.
Young shared a second-wicket stand of 78 in 18.4 overs with Parore after Craig Spearman had gone cheaply for six.
The two took the score to 104 when Parore was adjudged leg beforinner Mushtaq Ahmad. Young soon followed, losing his middle stump to a fiery Waqar Younis delivery at 117.
New Zealand scented victory when Fleming and Cairns joined to add 60 runs for the fourth wicket in just 9.4 overs.

Cairns was the more aggressive, slamming Younis and Shahid Afridi for a six each in a 28-ball innings that contained two fours. But he edged a catch to Moin Khan behind the stumps off Younis at 177 and eight runs later Fleming fell to Mushtaq, being stumped after 63 minutes at the wicket.
The visitors then succumbed to Mushtaq's wiles and though Chris Harris made a quick 20 off 11 balls, it was not enough.
Pakistan, batting first after winning the toss, were helped to a respectable total by half-centuries from Salim Malik and captain Wasim Akram.
Man-of-the-match Malik made an unbeaten 73. Wasim, playing his first match against the touring side, hit a lusty 52 to take his tally in one-day games past 2,000 runs in his 215th game.
The Pakistan captain smashed three sixes and as many fours, sharing a sixth wicket stand of 91 in 15.3 overs with Malik which rescued the side after five wickets had fallen for 71.
Malik's crisp innings included a six and six fours off 78 balls. It was his 41st half-century in his 247th one-day international.
Opener Saeed Anwar made 26 and became the fourth Pakistani to complete 4,000 one-day runs after Javed Miandad, Malik and Ramiz Raja.
